SUBJECT: ZONING CODE AMENDMENT TO MODIFY TITLE 11, CHAPTER 11.43 (ACCESSORY
DWELLING UNITS AND ACCESSORY STRUCTURES) OF THE SOUTH GATE MUNICIPAL CODE
AND FINDING THE ACTION EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY
ACT.

PURPOSE: To consider Resolution No. 2026-11 regarding a proposed Zone Code Amendment to Chapter 11.43
(Accessory Dwelling Units and Accessory Structures) of the South Gate Zoning Code (which is set forth in Title
11 of the South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC)), and making a recommendation to the City Council (“Council’)
that the City’s Zoning Code be revised to align with state law.

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS: Staff recommends that the Commission take the following actions:

  a. CONDUCT a public hearing;
  b. ACCEPT the determination that the Planning Commission’s action recommending adoption of the Zone
  Change Amendment (“ZCA”) is not subject to California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) review
  because it does not constitute an “approval” of the ZCA, as defined in CEQA Guidelines Section 15352,
  but rather a recommendation of approval that does not commit the City to any definite course of
  action regarding the ZCA; and
  c. FURTHER ACCEPT the determination that the ZCA is statutorily exempt from CEQA pursuant
  to Public Resources Code Section 21080.17 and CEQA Guidelines Section 15284(h), which
  exempt the adoption of an ordinance implementing the provisions of Government Code Sections 66314
  through 66339.5 (regulations regarding Accessory Dwelling Units and Junior Accessory Dwelling
  Units), and is additionally categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061(b)(3), because it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility the ZCA may have
  a significant effect on the environment; and
  d. APPROVE Resolution No. 2026-11 recommending approval of an Ordinance to the City Council
  to amend Chapter 11.43 (Accessory Dwelling Units and Accessory Structures) of the South Gate
  Zoning Code.

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION: Advertising and notification of the public hearing for this item was conducted in
compliance with SGMC Sections 11.50.020 and 11.50.030. Notice of the hearing was originally posted and
published in the “South Gate Press” on August 13, 2026.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: Many actions undertaken by the City of South Gate are subject to the
California Environmental Quality Act, a state law codified at Public Resources Code Sections 21000 through

  8
 21189.91 (“CEQA”), and related regulations enacted by the State Resources Agency codified at Title 14 of the
California Code of Regulations, Sections 15000 through 15387 (the “CEQA Guidelines”). An action defined as
a “project” under CEQA and the CEQA Guidelines is subject to compliance with CEQA, unless exempt or
otherwise not subject to review.

The Planning Commission’s action on Resolution 2026-11 is a recommendation of approval of the Zone Change
Amendment (“ZCA”) to the City Council, and does not itself constitute an “approval” of the ZCA as that term is
defined in CEQA Guidelines Section 15352, nor does it commit the City to any definite course of action regarding
the ZCA. Accordingly, the Planning Commission’s action is not subject to CEQA review.

Further, the ZCA is statutorily exempt from CEQA pursuant to Public Resources Code Section 21080.17 and
CEQA Guidelines Section 15284(h), which exempt the adoption of an ordinance implementing the provisions of
Government Code Sections 66314 through 66339.5 (regulations regarding Accessory Dwelling Units
and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units).

The ZCA is additionally categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3),
which applies to projects where it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility the activity in question
may have a significant effect on the environment. The ZCA does not involve physical changes to the environment
but rather amends the City’s Zoning Code to bring it into compliance with State law; since the proposed Ordinance
does not result in any direct or indirect physical changes to the environment, there is no possibility that it could
have a significant environmental impact.

BACKGROUND: In January 2021, the City of South Gate established Chapter 11.43 of the SGMC, which
allowed Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as required by former Government Code Section 65852.2.
Previously, ADUs were commonly referred to as "granny flats," "in-law suites," or "second dwelling units."
Subsequently, on September 23, 2025, City Council adopted Ordinance No. 2025-01-CC, updating SGMC
11.43 to comply with State legislation, which became effective on October 14, 2025. On March 16, 2026, the
Department of Housing and Community Development ("HCD") issued a finding letter (Attachment 3) regarding
Ordinance No. 2025-01-CC. Since that time, State law regarding ADUs and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units
(JADUs) has continued to be modified as new bills are signed into law by the Governor, including Assembly
Bill (AB) 130, Assembly Bill (AB) 462, Assembly Bill (AB) 1154, Senate Bill (SB) 543, and Senate Bill
(SB) 9. The proposed changes discussed below relate to these five bills and are now incorporated into SGMC
Chapter 11.43. The table below summarizes the content of the bills staff is proposing to codify.

  State Law Changes Affecting ADUs/ JADUs
 Bill  Effective Date  Summary
 AB 130  June 30, 2025  Existing law voids any covenant, restriction, or condition in a deed, contract,
  or other instrument that effectively prohibits or unreasonably restricts the
  construction or use of an ADU or JADU on a single-family lot, while still
  permitting reasonable restrictions that do not unreasonably increase
  construction cost or effectively prohibit construction. AB 130 prohibits fees
  and other financial requirements from being included among those
  “reasonable restrictions.”
  Existing law required a local agency that had adopted an ordinance by July
  1, 2018, allowing ADUs in multifamily dwelling structures to ministerially
  consider permit applications for specified ADU variations, and authorized

  9
   that agency to impose objective standards (design, development, historic
  standards, etc.) on those ADUs – except minimum lot size requirements. AB
  130 removes both the ministerial-consideration requirement and the
  authorization for the local agency to impose objective standards on that
  specific category of ADUs.
AB 462  October 10, 2025  Existing law prohibits a local agency from issuing a certificate of occupancy
  for an ADU before the primary dwelling receives its own certificate of
  occupancy. AB 462 creates an exception: a local agency must issue a
  certificate of occupancy for an ADU built in a county under a Governor’s
  state-of-emergency proclamation made on or after February 1, 2025, even if
  the primary dwelling hasn’t yet received its certificate of occupancy,
  provided certain conditions are met – including that the primary dwelling was
  substantially damaged or destroyed by the event reference in the emergency
  proclamation.
  AB 462 also includes findings that its changes address a matter of statewide
  concern rather than a municipal affair, making it applicable to all cities,
  including charter cities, and it took effect immediately as an urgency statute.
AB 1154  January 1, 2026  Existing law requires an ordinance authorizing JADUs to, among other
  things, require owner-occupancy in the single-family residence where the
  JADU is permitted. AB 1154 limits that owner-occupancy requirement so it
  applies only if the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the existing
  structure. In other words, a JADU with its own separate bathroom (not shared
  with the primary residence) would no longer trigger the owner-occupancy
  requirement. AB 1154 requires an ordinance authorizing JADUs to mandate
  that any rental of a JADU be for a term longer than 30 days – effectively
  prohibiting short-term/ vacation rental use of JADUs.
SB 543  January 1, 2026  Existing law defines a JADU as no more than 500 square feet in size,
  contained entirely within a single-family structure. SB 543 revises this to
  specify the 500-square-foot limit as interior livable space.
  Existing law already requires local agencies to submit ADU ordinances to
  HCD within 60 days for review, with ADU standards superseding conflicting
  local ordinances. SB 543 extends this same framework to JADU ordinances
  — requiring submission within 60 days, HCD notification of noncompliance,
  and nullification of the ordinance if the agency fails to submit it or respond
  to HCD's findings — and specifies that JADU standards likewise supersede
  conflicting local ordinances.
  If a local agency has not adopted a JADU ordinance, SB 543 requires JADU
  permit applications to be considered under the same ministerial approval
  process as ADUs, and prohibits any local ordinance/policy/regulation (other
  than a compliant JADU ordinance) from being used to delay or deny a JADU
  permit.
  SB 543 requires permitting agencies to determine whether an ADU or JADU
  application is complete and provide written notice within 15 business days of
  receipt. If incomplete, the agency must list the missing items and allow the
  applicant to cure. If an application is deemed incomplete or is denied, the
  agency must provide an appeal process, with a final written determination

  10
   required within 60 business days of receiving the appeal.
  Existing law prohibits impact fees on ADUs of 750 square feet or less and
  requires proportional fees above that threshold; it also restricts utility
  connection fees/charges for certain ADUs. SB 543 extends these same fee
  limitations to JADUs, revising the ADU threshold to be based on 750 square
  feet of interior livable space and the JADU threshold at 500 square feet of
  interior livable space.
  SB 543 specifies that an ADU or JADU with less than 500 square feet of
  interior livable space does not count toward the 500-square-foot assessable
  space threshold that triggers school facility fees.
  Existing law prohibits a local agency from capping ADU size below 850 sq
  ft (or 1,000 sq ft for more than one bedroom), and separately requires local
  agencies to permit at least an 800-square-foot ADU with 4-foot side/rear
  setbacks. SB 543 revises these size limitations to be based on interior livable
  space rather than the prior undefined "size" standard.
  SB543 requires ministerial approval of a building permit application for a
  combination of ADU and JADU on the same lot, revises the 800-square-foot
  floor area limit to be based on interior livable space, and extends the existing
  prohibition on requiring fire sprinklers (when not required for the primary
  residence) to JADUs as well.
 SB  9 January 1, 2026  Existing law requires a local agency to submit its ADU ordinance to the
 (2025)  Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) within 60 days
  of adoption. HCD may submit written findings on whether the ordinance
  complies with state standards, and if it finds noncompliance, must give the
  local agency up to 30 days to respond. If the local agency does not amend the
  ordinance or adopt a resolution explaining why it complies, existing law
  requires HCD to notify the local agency and authorizes HCD to notify the
  Attorney General of the violation. SB9 would invalidate the local agency’s
  ADU ordinance if the agency either fails to submit the ordinance to HCD
  within 60 days of adoption, or fails to respond to HCD’s noncompliance
  findings within the 30-day window.

ANALYSIS:

To align SGMC Chapter 11.43 with new State legislation, Staff proposes the following changes:
  1. Assembly Bill (AB) 130: Amending the chapter to reflect the State's prohibition on fees and other financial
  requirements being imposed as a condition on the sale, rental, or transfer of an ADU or JADU, consistent
  with the amendment to Civil Code Section 714.3.
  2. Assembly Bill (AB) 462: Amending the chapter to allow issuance of a certificate of occupancy for an
  ADU prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy for the primary dwelling, where the primary dwelling
  was substantially damaged or destroyed by an event referenced in a Governor-declared state of emergency
  proclaimed on or after February 1, 2025.
  3. Assembly Bill (AB) 1154: Amending the chapter to limit the owner-occupancy requirement for JADUs
  to only those instances where the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the existing primary dwelling,
  and to require that any JADU rental be for a term of more than thirty (30) days.
  4. Senate Bill (SB) 543: Amending the chapter to (a) define JADU and ADU size limitations by reference to

  11
   "interior livable space," (b) extend impact fee limitations to JADUs of five hundred square feet or less of
  interior livable space, and (c) require ministerial approval of combined ADU/JADU applications on
  single-family parcels.
  5. Senate Bill (SB) 9 Compliance Note: In addition to the code amendments described above, SB 9 requires
  a local agency to submit its ADU ordinance to the Department of Housing and Community Development
  ("HCD") within sixty (60) days of adoption for HCD's review. If HCD determines the ordinance does not
  comply with State standards, the local agency must respond to HCD's findings within thirty (30) days,
  either by amending the ordinance or adopting a resolution with findings explaining why the ordinance
  complies. SB 9 further provides that an ADU ordinance is invalidated if the local agency fails to timely
  submit the ordinance to HCD or fails to timely respond to HCD's noncompliance findings. SB 9 does not
  require any additional substantive amendment to Chapter 11.43; rather, it establishes a procedural
  compliance obligation. Staff will submit the amended ordinance to HCD within the required timeframe
  following adoption to ensure continued validity of the chapter.

Attachment 2 provides a detailed list of the proposed changes as they relate to aligning SGMC Chapter 11.43
with the latest ADU State laws. While Attachment 4A is an example of the revised municipal code.

CONCLUSION: Staff recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. 2026-11,
recommending approval of the amendments to SGMC Chapter 11.43 to Council.

11.43.010 Purpose and intent.
A.  This chapter (the “chapter”) establishes the standards for permitting Accessory Dwelling Units (“ADUs”)
within the City of South Gate, formerly known as “second dwelling units,” on residential properties in accordance
with Sections 66310 through 66342 and Sections 65852.27, and 65863.3 of the California Government Code, and
Section 714.3 of the California Civil Code, as amended and effective January 1, 2026. An Accessory Dwelling Unit
that conforms to the development and design standards in this chapter shall:

  1.  Be deemed an accessory use or an accessory building and not be considered to exceed the allowable
  density for the lot upon which it is located;

  2.  Be deemed a residential use that is consistent with the existing general plan and zoning designation for
  the lot upon which it is located;

  3.  Not be considered in the application of any ordinance, policy, or program to limit residential growth; and

  4.  Not be considered a new residential use for the purposes of calculating connection fees or capacity
  charges for utilities, including water and sewer service.

(Ord. 2025-01-CC § 1 (Exh. A), 10-14-25; Ord. 2021-01-CC § 3, 1-26-21)

11.43.020 Definitions.
For purposes of this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:

A.  “Accessory Dwelling Unit” or “ADU” means an attached or detached residential dwelling unit that provides
complete independent living facilities for one or more persons and is located on a lot with a proposed or existing
primary residence. It shall include permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation on the
same parcel as the primary dwelling is or will be situated. An Accessory Dwelling Unit also includes (i) an
efficiency unit, as defined in Section 17958.1 of the Health and Safety Code and (ii) a manufactured home, as
defined below and in Section 18007 of the Health and Safety Code. An ADU must be either (a) attached to, or
located within, the proposed or existing primary dwelling, including attached garages, storage areas or similar uses,
or an accessory structure, or (b) detached from the proposed or existing primary dwelling and located on the same
lot as the proposed or existing primary dwelling.

B.  “Accessory Dwelling Unit permit” means the formal, written approval of the community development
director approving the application for an Accessory Dwelling Unit.

C.  “Application” means an application for an Accessory Dwelling Unit permit.

D.  “Attached” means attached to the primary dwelling.

E.  “Building codes” means all of the requirements for authorization for the construction, alteration,
improvement, modification, demolition or removal of any structure within the City of South Gate, including all

11.43.010 Purpose and intent.
A.  This chapter (the “chapter”) establishes the standards for permitting Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunits
(“ADUsaccessory dwelling units”) within the cCity of South Gate, formerly known as “second dwelling units,” on
residential properties in accordance with Sections 66310 through 66342 and Sections 65852.27, and 65863.3 of the

11.43.050 Development standards.
An Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit may be attached to, or located within, the proposed or existing primary dwelling,
including attached garages, storage areas, or similar uses, or an accessory structure, or detached from the proposed
or existing primary dwelling and located on the same lot as the proposed or existing primary dwelling.

A.  Floor Area. The following floor area standards for Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunits apply:

  1.  The total floor area of an Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit shall not exceed eight hundred fifty square feet if
  the Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit has one bedroom or less, and shall not exceed one thousand square feet if the
  Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit has more than one bedroom. The maximum square footage limitations specified
  in the preceding sentence shall not apply to ADUs created under Government Code section 66323, subdivision
  (a)(4).

  2.  If the Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit is attached to an existing primary dwelling, the maximum total floor
  area of the Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit shall be limited to the smaller of (a) the square footage specified in
  subsection (A)(1) of this section, or (b) fifty percent of the total floor area of the existing primary dwelling.

  3.  Junior Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunits shall not exceed five hundred square feet.

B.  Lot Coverage. The following lot coverage standards for Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunits apply:

  1.  The first eight hundred square feet of either an attached or detached Aaccessory Ddwelling Uunit will not
  count towards the lot coverage of the subject property. Any additional footprint after eight hundred square feet
  will count towards the lot coverage of the property, and the lot coverage limits of the underlying zone shall
  apply.
